title: Borncity: Vortex and Cinder groups bypass MFA to steal mailbox, OneDrive and SharePoint data, citing Palo Alto researchers
date_note: Borncity's article gives only its publication day; the Palo Alto team is said to have analysed attacks from September 2026.
actor: Vortex and Cinder (names as used by the Palo Alto team, per Borncity)
summary: Borncity reports that Palo Alto Networks' security team analysed attacks from September 2026 by two groups it calls Vortex and Cinder. Vortex used adversary-in-the-middle phishing and registered its own MFA device after login; Cinder reused a session token from a persistent login, so no new Duo MFA prompt appeared. According to the article, both groups extracted data and then demanded ransom.
plain: Borncity, relaying Palo Alto researchers, says two groups got into Microsoft cloud accounts despite MFA, took data and demanded ransom. One registered its own MFA device; the other reused a login session.
exec: Per Borncity's account of the Palo Alto findings, MFA alone did not stop these data-theft and ransom attacks on Microsoft cloud accounts.
action: Palo Alto researchers recommend phishing-resistant MFA, verification of helpdesk requests, browser-extension allowlists and targeted revocation of existing sessions during incidents, per Borncity.
impact: Data taken from mailboxes, OneDrive and SharePoint, per the article; no victim count given.

validation.note: One publisher (Borncity) read; it relays Palo Alto researchers but links no original, and a search did not find their report naming Vortex.
